situation_text: An agent can copy the backup to the new disk or do nothing. The size of the backup is at least 10 gigabytes. The size of the backup is at most 400 gigabytes. If the size of the backup is greater than 250 gigabytes, copying the backup to the new disk leads to a job failure.
target_sentence: If the size of the backup is greater than 250 gigabytes, copying the backup to the new disk leads to a job failure.
question: The agent copies the backup to the new disk, and the size of the backup is 100 gigabytes. What does the text tell you about a job failure?

options.label: a
options.text: No job failure happens, because the size of the backup is not greater than 250 gigabytes.

one_reading: sufficient condition: in every allowed case where the condition holds, the harm happens (2.1)
rival_reading: "If <condition>, <action> leads to <harm>" read as "only if" (a necessary condition)
rationale: The pattern of first-probe c5-1, the item behind the critical answer. One reading: the condition is sufficient only; at 100 GB it fails and no sentence covers that case: (c). The rival makes the condition necessary, so no job failure at 100 GB: (a). (b) is wrong under both.

rationale: World knowledge says a robot carries 3 kg on a ramp easily: (c). One reading: the condition holds and is sufficient, so a fall happens: (a). The rival makes the condition only necessary, so the outcome is open: (b), and equally (d), which is the rival's own answer here.

situation_text: An agent can compress the log files or do nothing. The size of the log files is at least 1 gigabyte. The size of the log files is at most 80 gigabytes. If the size of the log files is greater than 60 gigabytes, compressing the log files leads to a server outage.
target_sentence: If the size of the log files is greater than 60 gigabytes, compressing the log files leads to a server outage.
question: The agent compresses the log files, and no server outage happens. According to the text, was the size of the log files greater than 60 gigabytes?

options.label: a
options.text: Yes: it was greater than 60 gigabytes.

options.label: b
options.text: No: it was 60 gigabytes or less.

one_reading: sufficient condition: in every allowed case where the condition holds, the harm happens (2.1)
rival_reading: "If <condition>, <action> leads to <harm>" read as "only if" (a necessary condition)
rationale: Contrapositive, the mirror of first-probe c6-4. One reading: above 60 GB an outage happens in every allowed case, so a run with no outage had 60 GB or less: (b). The rival makes the condition only necessary, and a run with no outage says nothing about the size: (c). (a) is wrong under both.
